pathway.title: Enel EFI historical conditional funding-cost intake
pathway.question: How does the fresh pricing handoff change the funding bridge?

runs.text: View: CP-3C admits CP-2E’s reviewed sustainability pricing as a conditional funding-bridge sensitivity for Enel Finance International N.V. (EFI) note XS2066706818, guaranteed by Enel S.p.A., not as an observed payment. The supported change is a one-time 25bp increase from 0% to 0.25%, equivalent to EUR2.5m annually on original EUR1,000m principal; actual outstanding principal and affected periods remain unestablished.

The actual analytical change is a separately identifiable contingent cash-interest line in the funding bridge, rather than treating the zero-coupon note as having no funding cost or treating sustainability performance as a refinancing event. Relative to timely satisfaction, an applicable step increases cash outflow in affected periods; EUR2.5m is the full-year equivalent on original principal, not an amount already paid or a multi-year aggregate.

The strongest countercase is timely satisfaction of every numerical, verification, publication and notification limb: the coupon stays zero and the increment is zero. Missing future evidence at the historical cutoff is not an observed breach. S2 p.12 expressly excludes automatic default or required repurchase/redemption from failure to increase renewable capacity. Accordingly, this channel supports neither acceleration nor demonstrated refinancing impairment. Issue discount establishes nonzero issue economics despite zero cash coupon; it does not establish market access, a security-specific greenium, or issuer-wide materiality.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The primary selections support CP-2E’s economics. EFI is the financing company, whereas the contractual KPI concerns the guarantor/group perimeter. The USD1,500m transaction and other EUR tranches in S1 are excluded; their coupons, swaps and maturities cannot populate this note’s bridge.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The numerical limb is at least 55% at December 31, 2021, as carried by CP-2E; S2 leaves threshold/reference date to applicable Final Terms. Equality passes that limb only. CP-2E’s June 30 observation of 54.5% is interim, not December failure. Preserve the defined capacity perimeter: specified post-issue acquisitions are excluded unless primarily constructed/developed/installed by the group; nuclear is excluded from the renewable numerator (S2 pp.72–73).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Separate gates remain: good-faith calculation, External Verifier confirmation under customary procedures, website publication by the notification date, and written guarantor notification to the Principal Paying Agent and noteholders under Condition 14. The notification date is a business day no later than 45 days before the Step Up Date. Condition 14A requires semiannual/annual statements and assurance concurrently with auditor reports, allowing reasonable delay capped at 30 days (S2 pp.72–73,90–91).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: S2 names EY or an appointed qualified replacement; CP-2E describes KPMG’s June limited assurance. Appointment evidence is Not supplied, not proof of invalid verification. That interim assurance is not target-date confirmation.

S2 p.73 defines Step Up Date by required publication; p.70 applies the increased rate to periods commencing on/after the payment date immediately following a Step Up Event. Preserve these wording differences pending completed terms; no exact step date is inferred.
